threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused at the bus stop when the driver waves you past. Locals know you just hop on anywhere, mate.
Caught a night bus from Brixton the other week; two blokes started arguing over who had the loudest Spotify playlist. It was like a mini rave in the back.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted an old man feeding pigeons outside the Türkischer Markt, I realized this place breathes culture, history, and a touch of chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you watch a techno DJ mix while waiting for your bus at 6 AM on a Sunday. It's all part of the rich, chaotic tapestry here.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone's local when they can name all the taco trucks and still find a new one that just popped up last week.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading commuters with an accordion while the 47 sat idle at Jones. For a moment, it felt like a scene straight out of a movie.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists keep asking where the 'real Gràcia' is, completely missing the fact that the vibe changes every hour with locals just living their lives.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for directions to places like Parc Güell while clutching a map instead of using their phones. You spot them in the same cafes every day.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'the underground'—everyone knows it's a city thing, not just a Hackney thing.
Last night on the 12, a lad argued passionately about 'the best kebab' while holding a half-eaten one. The driver just nodded along.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was really home when I spotted a guy selling handmade pierogi from his bike. Only in Neukölln would you find such a gem on a Tuesday afternoon.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you stumble into a hidden 'Kaffeeklatsch' at a courtyard, where locals gather to swap stories over home-brewed coffee. It’s intimate and authentically Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they know the exact time to avoid BART delays. Tourists just wait cluelessly at Civic Center.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy juggling on the 47 bus yesterday. He dropped a ball, and it bounced clean into the lap of a sleeping passenger. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'poble' means village, but here it means community—check the local scenes, not just the tourist haunts.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer in Gràcia by their enthusiasm for pa amb tomàquet — it’s the only thing they order before they realize it’s not a breakfast item.
